gap: No result ChatGPT got states what an off-grid inverter costs per watt of continuous output at today's prices across brands, or how much of a 48 V battery its idle draw uses each day. At today's prices that is $0.16/W for the Sun Gold Power SPH6548P ($1,035 / 6,500 W) against $0.25/W for the EG4 6000XP ($1,499.99 / 6,000 W). The EG4's 30 W best-case idle draw would use about 14% of a 5.12 kWh battery per day.
standout_why: I compared against the cited EG4 6000XP maker page, wildjoule.com/best-off-grid-inverter (2026-10-17) and storyofsolar.com's 2026 ranking. The EG4 page gives a 30 W idle figure but no price and no daily energy. Wildjoule turns idle draw into kWh per day (EG4 1.2 kWh at ~50 W, Victron 0.46 kWh) but shows no prices and lists the SPH6548P idle draw as 'Not published'. Storyofsolar gives price ranges (EG4 $1,499–$1,899, Victron $1,300–$2,200) but no idle figures and no Sun Gold Power models. None of them gives cost per continuous watt at today's store prices across brands, or idle loss as a share of a battery. Idle kWh per day alone would score only 1, because wildjoule already has it.
decides: Dealectric lists the Sun Gold Power SPH6548P (affiliate link), and on cost per continuous watt it beats ChatGPT's top pick by about 36% ($0.159/W against $0.250/W). Both are 48 V, 120/240 V split-phase units with two MPPTs. The EG4 6000XP still has the published idle figure, and on an off-grid battery that is a daily cost: 0.72 kWh, or 14% of a 5.12 kWh pack. I could not source the SPH6548P's idle draw, so the page can call it the cheapest per watt but cannot yet say it wins on total daily energy.
